title: Features of the influence of affective stimuli on human emotional activity
abstract: Objective: to study the autonomic correlates of emotional reactions when viewing affective images based on the theory of information representations/images, and to determine their relationship with the level of emotional maladjustment. Methods and materials. The event-related telemetry method was used to assess the dynamics of the subjects' functional state. The level of emotional maladjustment was assessed using the Grigoriev and Tkhostov projective technique. The SAM self-assessment test was used to analyze the subjects' subjective emotional response to stimulus images. Results. Two types of autonomic responses were identified among participants who demonstrated a standard subjective evaluation of affective stimuli according to the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM). In 53% of the participants, an adequate autonomic response was observed, in which positive stimuli were associated with an improvement in functional state, reflected by an increase in adaptive potential and a decrease in the stress index. In the remaining 47% of the participants, a paradoxical autonomic response was identified, in which positive stimuli were associated with a deterioration of functional state. An association was found between the type of autonomic response and the level of emotional maladjustment, particularly with respect to the need for safety. Conclusions. The results suggest that the nature of the autonomic response to stimuli is related to the level of emotional maladjustment in the subjects. This approach allows for the assessment of the dynamics of functional state within a single experimental session by continuously recording physiological indicators using event-related telemetry. This enabled the recording of changes in the state of each subject in response to the presentation of stimuli of different valence without the need for repeated measurements on different days.
